resources.string: Killit can unblock every app you have blocked, so it stays locked.
Wrong passkey. %1$d attempts left before a lockout.
Too many attempts. Try again in %1$s.
This passkey protects Killit itself. Anyone who gets past it can unblock your apps.
Killit can block and unblock apps.
Killit cannot block anything until it is provisioned as Device Owner. Pick one of the three ways below.
Removing Killit is not immediate. Pressing this starts a countdown; only once it has finished can the apps be unblocked and Killit give up Device Owner. You can cancel at any point during the wait.
Killit can be removed in %1$s. Until then everything stays blocked.
The waiting period is over. Killit can now unblock everything and give up Device Owner.
Every blocked app will be unblocked first, then Killit gives up its Device Owner privileges. Re-provisioning needs a factory reset. Continue?
All three methods need a device with no accounts signed in and no existing device owner. On a device already in use that means a factory reset.
Connect this phone to a computer to turn on protection.
Turn on USB debugging in Developer options, then plug this phone into a computer.
Run this command on the computer:
When it prints Success, come back here and tap Refresh status.
Use the free Shizuku app to turn on protection.
Install Shizuku and start it over wireless debugging.
Come back here and tap the button below.
Grant Shizuku permission when it asks.
Shizuku is not running. Start it first.
This Shizuku version is too old. Update it.
Provision this phone from the Android setup wizard.
On the welcome screen, tap the same spot 6 times to open the QR scanner.
Scan the code from the Killit website. The phone downloads and provisions Killit in one step.
Show packages without a launcher icon

Stops Killit being removed to escape the block.
Greys out Force stop in Settings, and blocks Clear data too on Android 13 or newer. Needs Android 11 or newer.
Safe mode would otherwise disable third-party apps on reboot.
Block factory reset and new users
Closes the last bypass routes. adb stays available as the only way out.

Off by default, because it applies to every app on the device: you would not be able to uninstall, force-stop or clear data for any of them, not just the blocked ones. Killit\'s own data is already protected without it.
The removal countdown is measured against the clock. Without this it can be skipped by moving the date forward.

Every one of them has to approve before this device opens.
%1$s has to approve being removed — you will need that phone in front of you. This is the only way to undo a pairing.
%1$s scans this to approve being removed. %2$s left.
Point the camera at the approval code on their screen. %1$s left.
This cannot be undone on your own

Once this device has a companion:

• Your PIN, pattern or password stops working. The only way in is a companion approving from their phone, in person.
• Every companion must approve — not just one.
• Removing Killit becomes unavailable until all companions are removed.
• Removing a companion needs that companion's approval.

If a companion phone is lost, wiped or reinstalled, this device can no longer be opened and Killit can no longer be removed. The only remaining option is a factory reset from Recovery Mode, which erases everything on it.
Pairing works one way. Adding a companion here changes nothing on their phone, and them adding you changes nothing on yours.
You scan their code. This phone will then open only with their approval.
They scan your code. This phone is not locked and does not change.
Once you scan their code, this phone will need their approval every time it opens. The other phone does not change.
The phone that scans this code is the one that gets locked. Nothing on this phone changes.
On the other phone open Killit, go to Companion devices and tap “Show my code”. Then come back here.
Point the camera at the code on the other phone\'s screen.
This phone opens only with companion approval from now on.
Have the other phone scan this. Nothing on this phone changes.
Show a code to your companions and scan what they show back. All %1$d must approve.
Someone else needs your approval to open their phone. This does not open yours.
On their phone: Killit → Approve another phone. Once they have scanned it, tap below.
Point the camera at the approval code on their screen.
This request ran out of time.
Point the camera at the code on the phone that needs opening. Approving does not open this phone.
Hold this up to the phone that needs opening.
That is a Killit code, but not the one this screen is waiting for.
That request has expired. Start a new one.
That approval did not check out.
That phone is not a companion of this device.
This device has no pairing identity. Its data may have been cleared.
Pairing needs Device Owner, so it cannot be undone by clearing app data.
That phone is already a companion.
A device cannot be its own companion.

%1$d device(s) can only be opened with this phone\'s approval, and the key that gives it lives here and nowhere else. Removing Killit, uninstalling it or clearing its data would destroy that key and leave those devices unopenable — a factory reset from Recovery Mode would be all they had left. Those devices have to remove this phone as a companion first.

Apps are still blocked, but the passkey is gone, so Killit cannot verify who you are. It will not unblock anything in this state.\n\nTo recover, remove Killit as Device Owner from a computer. That releases every blocked app:
Killit is now the Device Owner of this device.
